issue.title: ToolRun retention never prunes stage rows: stage stamps are epoch ms, detail cutoff is epoch seconds
issue.description:
Found while planning the `sase tool` TUI surfaces epic (verifying ToolRun stage data units).

`apply_retention` in sase-core computes `detail_cut` in epoch **seconds**
(`now.saturating_sub(detail_days * 86400)`), then prunes stage rows with
`COALESCE(s.finished_ts, s.started_ts, 0) < ?1`. But `stages.started_ts` / `finished_ts`
are stored in epoch **milliseconds**: the `tools/_run_silent_record.py` producer writes
ms stamps and `StageIngestor` / `lifecycle.rs` (stage upsert, ~lines 837-881) store them
unchanged. A 13-digit ms value is never below a 10-digit seconds cutoff, so the
detail-age pruning of `stages` is a no-op. Samples, events, and triage rows use
seconds and do prune.

Fix: compare stage stamps against `detail_cut * 1000` (or normalize in one helper),
add a retention test with a settled run whose stages are older than `detail_days`, and
check `retention_preview` reports the same counts. Do not change the stored unit (the
TUI/CLI readers already treat stage stamps as ms).

task_type_fields.impact: The stages table is only pruned with its run at the 180-day summary horizon instead of the 60-day detail horizon, so ~/.sase/tools/runs.sqlite grows beyond its documented bound (about 8 stage rows per run, ~1.3k runs/week on athena). No data loss.
task_type_fields.repro:
Read-only on any host with a ledger:

    python3 -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:'+__import__('os').path.expanduser('~/.sase/tools/runs.sqlite')+'?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select started_ts,finished_ts from stages order by rowid desc limit 2').fetchall(), c.execute('select created_ts from events order by rowid desc limit 1').fetchall())"

On athena (2026-09-27) stages hold `1790547674615`-style values (ms) while events hold
`1790547707` (s). Then read `crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/store/retention.rs` (the
`DELETE FROM stages ... COALESCE(s.finished_ts, s.started_ts, 0) < ?1` bound to the
seconds `detail_cut`).

issue.creation_reason: Discovered while verifying ToolRun stage data for the sase tool TUI epic plan; the 60-day detail horizon silently never applies to the stages table, so it grows for the full 180-day summary window.
